title: Adaptive refinement of a plane wave on a perfectly conducting sphere (radius 5 mm, ka = 1.05) at 10 GHz: passes from three elements per wavelength until the far field changes by less than 2 %
source: The Mie series of a perfectly conducting sphere, aₙ = ψₙ'(ka)/ξₙ'(ka), bₙ = ψₙ(ka)/ξₙ(ka) (J. A. Stratton, Electromagnetic Theory, 1941, §9.25; C. F. Bohren, D. R. Huffman, 1983, §4.4), evaluated by emcraft-theory::radiation independently of the finite elements

quantities.quantity: scattering cross-section (mm²), solved on the adapted mesh
quantities.reason: the far field changes by 2.8e-2 and 1.4e-2 at passes 2 and 3 (19 660, 27 962, 62 530 unknowns), the loop stopping at 3: +0.51 %. Uniform meshes: +2.4 % at five elements per wavelength (53 090 unknowns), +1.0 % at six (92 528, pec-sphere-scattering): the adapted mesh halves the error with two thirds of the unknowns. A fourth pass (156 142 unknowns) stays at +0.6 %: what is left is the layer's and the Huygens box's quadrature
